Use case: identity-preserve. Asset: a transparent sprite-animation strip for an existing gritty 2D fighting game. Image1 is the EXACT approved idle model, identity, proportions, clothing colors, hatching and boots. Image2 is the same approved character in another action, only to clarify shoulder/face/clothes consistency. Draw the SAME man and SAME original rough ink art; do not redesign or beautify him. Short spiky light-brown hair, ugly angular clenched face, wrinkled dusty maroon-brown short-sleeved T-shirt, loose muted reddish-brown trousers with their existing folds and seams, dark heavy laced ankle boots. Keep identical garment material hues, dark line weight and diagonal crosshatching, matte flesh, no glossy comic superhero finish. Facing screen RIGHT, full-body three-quarter fighting-game view as reference, looking at the target. No opponent, effects, speed lines, target, labels, floor, cast shadow, backdrop, frame, grid or text. True transparent alpha.
OUTPUT: exactly TWO equal cells placed horizontally, no overlap. Ideal canvas1000x550, each cell500x550, left cell CHAMBER, right cell CONTACT, both drawn at exactly the same body scale as reference. The ground line within each cell is y523; keep head size and supporting boot consistent. Keep 12px empty margin around the full silhouette; neither boot nor fist may cross its cell. Each cell contains exactly one complete man, exactly2 arms and2 legs, no extra limbs. Original idle is NOT redrawn; it will be reused by the game. Only produce chamber and contact.
Motion continuity: same supporting leg in both drawings, natural visible support knee and ankle, same face and hair, fists retain guard while torso and pelvis participate modestly. Natural thigh and shin lengths; knee hinge connects hip and ankle with no double joints. Keep head following a small chest turn, not thrown backward. It must look like a brutal compact street kick, no ballet, extreme split, spin or jump.

variants.a-front: A: FRONT KICK to abdomen with the LEAD leg (leg whose boot is farther to screen right in idle). The REAR leg remains planted. LEFT CELL: raise lead knee compactly to waist level, lower leg folded underneath knee, fists guarding chin, body upright. RIGHT CELL: extend that same lead leg forward, boot striking with ball/sole into a target at waist/abdomen height. Toe lifted naturally, knee softly bent rather than hyperextended. Torso leans slightly back as a whole but head stays aligned with spine and watches right. Rear supporting boot remains under the weight and planted on the same spot. Strong forward thrust, not a high head kick. Avoid making the raised knee float disconnected from hip or stretching the calf.
variants.b-side: B: SIDE HEEL KICK to torso using the LEAD leg (leg whose boot is farther right in idle). REAR leg remains planted. LEFT CELL: lead knee folded across in front of belly, hip turns slightly side-on, a compact chamber for a side kick; fists still defend chin. RIGHT CELL: drive heel sharply toward screen right at waist/lower-rib height, leg extending diagonally a little upward, sole/heel facing target, toes flexed naturally a little downward. A modest coordinated turn of hips, chest and head, chest still seen3/4, not a full back view. Supporting knee slightly flexed and boot pivots realistically; rear support contact stays fixed. Body inclines slightly away but not a horizontal acrobatic lean. Leg is strong and anatomically proportioned, no enormous boot or unnaturally long thigh. This silhouette must clearly differ from a front kick: hip opens sideways and heel leads.
variants.c-low: C: LOW ROUND KICK to outer thigh using the REAR leg (leg whose boot is farther left in idle). The LEAD leg (front/right boot) stays planted and bears weight. LEFT CELL: rear knee lifts a little and begins a compact hip turn, bent rear shin behind/inward, lead supporting knee flexed; fists guard. RIGHT CELL: rear leg swings out toward screen right into opponent thigh height (boot well below the belt), shin angled gently down toward target, knee naturally slightly bent; a low round kick, not a front stomp. The entire pelvis/torso rotate a modest amount together and supporting boot pivots, eyes stay on target. Keep boot and ankle connected and natural. No knee hyperextension, full spin, backwards head, straight split or airborne supporting foot. Clearly two legs, including the grounded forward support boot and the swinging rear leg.
